title: WF03 Stage11 releasefix rework1: deterministic integration run exposes ADP-09/ADP-10 assertion failures (no stall)
summary: After supervised single-run execution, zig build test-integration completed deterministically and reported 6 failing tests. The releasefix blocker is no longer a hang; remaining failures are concrete assertion regressions in ADP integration suites.

root_cause.details: adp09_tamper_evident_audit_chain_test and adp10_agent_io_capture_audit_test assertions fail under deterministic full-suite execution.
root_cause.reassessment_20260811: Re-investigated directly against the current codebase (2026-08-11, run WF03-GH283-20260811) using the scoped `zig build test-integration-adp09`/`test-integration-adp10` build steps added by GH-679/ISS-0658 specifically to give this issue an isolated signal. Both test files already use TestHarness (helpers.zig), which has held the cross-binary advisory lock since PR #494 (GH-486/ISS-0162) and was extended to the remaining 31 self-managed-pool integration files by GH-681/ISS-0659 (merged PR #684, 2026-08-10). ADP-09 (5/5 test cases: TC-ADP-09-01 through -05) and ADP-10 (2/2 test cases: TC-ADP-10-01, -02) both passed cleanly and deterministically across 3 consecutive isolated runs each (6 total clean runs, 0 failures, 0 flakes). The original 2026-05-29 failure was captured under the old, unstable aggregate `zig build test-integration` suite, run concurrently with ~30 other test binaries with no mutual exclusion over shared audit_entries/tenant rows -- i.e. it was a concurrency/contention symptom of the same class ISS-0658/ISS-0659 root-caused and fixed, not a genuine logic defect in the tamper-evident chain or agent-IO-capture code paths themselves. No source code change to src/ was required or made; the fix that resolved this issue's actual behavior already landed via GH-679/GH-681. A prior 2026-07-29 'LIKELY_FIXED' auto-triage note on this issue is disregarded -- it cited evidence from an unrelated SIM-05..08 release decision file, not SIM-01..04, and was never a valid basis for closing this issue.

resolution.description: No direct code fix required in this run. Confirmed the ADP-09/ADP-10 assertion failures reported in May 2026 no longer reproduce, as a side effect of GH-679 (ISS-0658, added scoped test-integration-adp09/-adp10 build steps + fixed an unrelated iss105 schema-scoping bug) and GH-681 (ISS-0659, extended TestHarness's PR #494 advisory-lock protection to 31 previously-unprotected integration test files). ADP-09 and ADP-10 were already TestHarness-based and therefore already covered by PR #494's original lock scope -- the fix that resolved their instability was GH-679's act of wiring them into a runnable (scoped) build step at all, since before that commit these two files were not registered in build.zig under ANY step, aggregate or scoped, and could not produce a signal in isolation from the unstable aggregate suite.

verification.notes: This machine (workspace r-co-2) has no local psql client installed, which tools/clean_test_db.py's direct-BPM_TEST_DB_URL mode shells out to; the docker-compose exec fallback path also could not be reached because Python's subprocess.run([...], shell=False) uses Windows CreateProcess directly, which does not perform PATHEXT (.cmd/.bat) resolution the way cmd.exe does. Worked around locally for this verification session only by compiling a small psql.exe forwarder (zig cc) in the session scratchpad directory that rewrites the host-mapped DB URL (localhost:5453) to the container-internal address (localhost:5432) and execs `docker exec -i r-co-2-db_test-1 psql`. This was a local-machine-only workaround for running the verification commands in this session; no repository files were touched by it and it is not part of this issue's resolution or files_changed.
verification.ci_coverage_gap_noted: No CI job in .github/workflows/ci.yml currently runs zig build test-integration-adp09 or -adp10 specifically (grep found no reference). Not fixed in this run -- out of this issue's scope per CLAUDE.md's Unblock-Everything boundary (adjacent, not blocking) -- but worth a follow-up if these tests should have dedicated CI coverage rather than relying on the (currently unstable, per ISS-0659 followup) aggregate suite.

prevention: Keep supervised deterministic integration evidence on every release-fix rerun.
Route deterministic failing suites directly to BACKEND-DEV with exact failing test IDs.

Do not trust an auto-triage 'LIKELY_FIXED' note without checking which evidence file it actually cites -- this issue's own 2026-07-29 note cited the wrong release-decision file (SIM-05..08 instead of SIM-01..04) and stayed uncaught for two weeks.

When an integration test's instability turns out to be environmental/concurrency-driven rather than a logic bug, prefer scoped build steps (test-integration-<slug>) to get a clean isolated signal rather than repeatedly re-running the full unstable aggregate suite.
